title: The widows' colony
hookLine: widows of November 1984 were resettled in one Delhi colony and raised children alone

lines: A UNIFORM, A LUNCH, A BUS STOP.
cards: A school uniform hangs on a nail. A mother irons it before dawn, packs a lunch, walks a child to the bus stop, and then goes to work. Plenty of households run on mornings like that.
In one neighborhood in West Delhi, street after street of those mornings were run by women alone, because their husbands, brothers and grown sons had been killed in a few days in November.
The government gave them flats there. People began calling the place by a name that stuck: the widows' colony.

teach.b: First, the November. After Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was shot by two of her Sikh bodyguards, mobs went through Delhi and other cities hunting Sikh men. Homes were burned.

Men were beaten and burned in front of their families. Survivors and later inquiries said the police often stood by, and some officials and politicians were accused of leading the mobs. Second, the colony.

Widows and their children from neighborhoods the mobs had struck were given flats in Tilak Vihar, in West Delhi. Women who had never earned a wage took jobs, often humble ones, to keep children fed and in school.
Third, the long after. Some children grew up angry and without work; some fell into drugs; others studied hard and climbed out. The mothers went to court, again and again, to testify.
Justice moved slowly, and for some families it still feels unfinished. Fourth, the root.

teach.h: ANG 473: FROM HER, KINGS ARE BORN.
teach.b: In Asa di Var, at Ang 473, Guru Nanak asks why anyone would call woman lesser, when from her kings are born. The women of the colony were not given a choice about becoming the head of a household.

But they carried it, and the gurbani they heard in their gurdwara had already said they were never lesser. The colony's real story isn't the days of the killing. It's the long run of ordinary mornings after it.

how: Sikhs remember the November killings each year in gurdwaras and at gatherings in Delhi, and Sikh groups have supported the widows and children of Tilak Vihar with schooling, work and help through the courts.

games.q: your husband was killed in November. you've been given a flat in a new neighborhood, and you have children to feed. what do you do?
o: move back to your family's village.
take whatever work you can and keep the children in school.

practice: Someone is raising a child mostly alone tonight; bring one such person to mind, a neighbor, a coworker, a cousin, your own parent once.
Breathe in and picture one of their ordinary mornings, the alarm, the lunch, the rush, and breathe out wishing them strength for it. If you pray, hold them in Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Widows' colony. The name people gave to Tilak Vihar in West Delhi, where widows of November were resettled and raised their children alone. Today's word.
